reading.body:
Tome is recorded here as a single product, an AI presentation and storytelling tool, with one MCP integration for customer data analysis.

The data covers a company entry and nothing more. There is no funding, headcount, revenue, model provider, or infrastructure detail, so nothing here speaks to compute, buildings, or power. The one integration listed, ai.saifs/customer-intelligence, points at sales segmentation rather than at the presentation product itself, which suggests the tool is being wired into a customer workflow rather than used only for slide generation.

What the entry does not tell the reader is scale. A single product and a single integration are consistent with an early company and with a narrow public listing, and this data cannot distinguish between them. It also gives no date for when the product or integration appeared, only the date the record was built.

For AI specifically, the useful signal is category. Presentation generation sits in the application layer, where value comes from interface and output quality rather than from owned compute. That layer is the least exposed to the grid constraint and the most exposed to whatever model access it rents. Nothing in this record shows which models Tome uses or where they run.
